newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Strike affects Israeli airport, shuts ports.
newsitem.headline: Strike affects Israeli airport, shuts ports.

text.p: Thousands of Israeli workers protesting against planned cuts in government spending staged a one-day strike on Thursday, disrupting international flights and shutting down seaports, officials said.
All outgoing flights were cancelled at Ben Gurion airport. Incoming flights were being allowed to land but airport workers were not unloading baggage, an airport spokesman said.
The strike also closed Haifa, Ashdod and Eilat seaports, and disrupted train and phone services.

The Histadrut labour federation said it planned strikes in other sectors in coming days, and threatened to stage a general strike on Tuesday when parliament is due to pass the government's controversial 1997 budget.
The Histadrut called the strike in response to cuts in government spending that union leaders said would hurt the poor.

"Unfortunately, the rules of the game have been violated. We wanted to be in favour of the government...but the workers feel someone is waiting for them at the corner," said Histadrut leader Amir Peretz.
Peretz, a member of parliament from the opposition Labour party, said the cuts would sharply erode workers' salaries.

The government's 1997 budget proposal includes seven billion shekels ($2.15 billion) in spending cuts and new taxes and other revenue measures that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyhau has said are necessary to rein in the deficit.
The budget must be passed in parliament by the end of the month.
But legislator Silvan Shalom, of the ruling Likud party, said most measures affecting the poor had been eliminated from the budget proposal during parliamentary debate.
"I don't exactly know what they're striking about. If they're talking about decrees we succeeded...in cancelling most of the decrees," Shalom told Israel Radio.

In a petition on Wednesday to the National Labour Court seeking a restraining order against the Histadrut, the Israel Manufacturers Association termed the action a "political strike" aimed at the Likud-led government.
